reason: Both reached the correct hidden cause (the 'washer' switch above the worktop) in the same number of turns and confirmed the fix, so the outcome was equal. Conversation 1 got there with tight, UK-appropriate questions (socket test, then switched spur) and stayed inside the safety boundary, its only blemish being an unnecessary model-number/replacement-part panel before the fix was confirmed. Conversation 2 opened with a long US-centric dump (GFCI outlets, breaker panel, garage) that didn't fit the homeowner, and told her to prise open the spur and swap its fuse with a screwdriver despite her having no tools and the boundary advising against opening the spur; its genuine pluses were the landlord-responsibility note and the burning-smell/leak check. On balance Conversation 1 was the more efficient and better-targeted help.
